AboutPage.title: About Me - Max Zhang
AboutPage.heading: About Me
AboutPage.status: Open to AI PM roles · Chengdu / Remote
AboutPage.description:
Now I'm turning ten years of engineering experience toward AI product: from "how to build it" to "who is it for, what should it do, and what success looks like."

2016. First job. I got lucky.

The company was already flat back then. Management, tech, and product leadership mostly had overseas backgrounds. The CTO didn't split roles by frontend and backend — one business direction, one person, full ownership from frontend to database to deployment. Later I'd learn this is called an Ownership culture. At the time I didn't realize how unusual it was. I thought all companies worked this way.

First task: build a resource system. No mentor, no broken-down tickets. Started from '<input type="file">' and a blank editor. How PHP handles file uploads, how S3 stores them, whether PostgreSQL should use bytea or URLs — every step was figured out by running into a wall and reading through it.

Later, a hospital equipment data platform. PHP7 wasn't officially released yet, so I pulled the PHP source and compiled it myself with cmake. The hospital's internal network ran Windows, logs needed forwarding to Linux, and the SMB protocol was the blocker. PHP had no native support for it, so I dug into libsmbclient's C library docs and compiled a PHP extension module. From C to PHP to the protocol layer — one chain punched through. Felt good when it worked.

Then Yixin Cloud 2.0. Delivered on time, right on the company's demo and fundraising timeline. No delays.

Looking back, that period left me with a habit: goal set, walk it end to end. TypeScript, Go, Python. Docker, K8s, AWS. MCP, A2A, ReAct. The tools kept changing. The habit didn't.

That's why I care about Agents. Not chasing trends. I spent ten years waiting for something that amplifies one person's will. I used to run a chain with two hands. Now I write intent into a spec, a group of Agents executes. They're faster, but I set the direction, draw the boundaries, judge the results.

Not replacement. Leverage.

In the AI First era, tools are getting faster, but no one grows your sense of direction or judgment for you. Define the problem. Deliver end to end. Own the result. These haven't changed. Here's to building together.

experience.company: Chengdu Ruisheng Tianhe Media Technology Co., Ltd.
points: Led the productization of our multi-agent collaboration system: turned ad asset production into an orchestrated agent workflow across planning, generation, and review, with MCP for dynamic tool access.
Designed task dispatch and result aggregation for an A2A distributed agent network, so planning and execution agents can complete complex work together.
Built Docker sandbox isolation so agents can safely execute shell commands, Python, and browser automation.

Led the company's digital advertising platform, connecting asset production, approvals, campaign delivery, and data feedback into an online workflow, supporting 100,000 videos and 30,000+ images per month with 80%+ efficiency gains.

Pioneered AI-native engineering workflows — integrated Codex, Claude, and in-house MCP to automate requirement drafting, task breakdown, execution validation, and bug fixing, reducing per-video generation cost from RMB 2.5–3 to RMB 0.5–1.
Drove engineering governance across several legacy internal systems (build upgrades, component refactors, monorepo, standards) to keep product iteration fast.
Worked across international, multi-line teams on requirement discovery, breakdown, and delivery, contributing to the evolution from modular to microservice architecture.
Maintained and iterated 20+ legacy projects, driving incremental refactors under high technical debt across React Native, Vue, React, Nest.js, PHP, and MongoDB.
Led a four-person team rewriting a high-traffic user-facing product area, adding RBAC, JWT auth, multi-environment config, global exception handling, and rate limiting.
Participated in microservice and distributed-systems work covering health checks, circuit breaking, Consul, Docker, SMS, caching, email, and scheduled tasks.
Owned the BD Policy Manager web app and WeChat H5 product end to end: worked directly with clients to translate business needs into product and engineering solutions.
Built a distributed crawler stack with Python, Scrapy, Redis, and Django, ingesting millions of insurance clauses.

Handled product demos and client presentations for hundreds of participants, and established a training pipeline that turned interns with no experience into independent contributors within six months.

experience.company: Chengdu Shulian Yixin Technology Co., Ltd.
points: Worked on hospital device data cleansing and forwarding systems, owning end-to-end delivery of Yixin Cloud Service resources from frontend to backend.
Enabled SMB support in PHP7 by compiling a C module, which made Windows log forwarding from hospital intranets to Linux systems possible.
Contributed to the SaaS platform and WeChat H5 apps, and helped deliver Yixin Cloud Service 2.0 on schedule for key product and fundraising milestones.
